market: ES (traded as MES); signal from Cboe daily VIX and VIX3M closes via bar['daily'] (prior session's close, published after 16:15 ET). VIX is computed from SPX options, so ES is the matched contract.
hypothesis: The weekday-adjusted 1-day change in VIX/VIX3M at the prior close predicts the sign of today's ES RTH return (09:35 -> 15:55): when the curve steepened back toward contango (ratio fell, |z| >= Z) go long; when it inverted further (ratio rose) go short. This beats random-direction trades in the same sessions with the same stop.
mechanism: Johnson (2017): the VIX term-structure slope measures the price of variance risk; a low/inverted slope predicts positive next-day returns on variance assets (variance swaps, VIX futures, straddles). Variance-asset returns and equity returns are strongly negatively correlated, so a further inversion (variance risk getting pricier) would point to equity weakness and a steepening back toward contango to relief. This bridge is an inference, not a documented equity result.

sources.summary: Johnson (2017, JFQA 52(6), 2461-2490), 'Risk Premia and the VIX Term Structure': the second principal component (SLOPE) summarizes nearly all variance-risk-premium information in the VIX term structure; it predicts returns on S&P 500 variance swaps, VIX futures and straddles, incremental to other VRP proxies. It is about the price of variance risk, not expected VIX changes.

CXO summary of Johnson: when the slope is very low, average next-day returns of the variance assets are positive in 17 of 18 asset-maturity cases; returns are gross. The 2011 job-market version was titled 'Equity Risk Premia and the VIX Term Structure'; the published paper reports variance-asset (not equity) predictability.
Practitioner reference (not evidence): VIX/VIX3M < 1 is normal contango; a sustained rise above 1 marks an inverted, risk-off curve. No return claim.

sources_equity_direction: Searched for a study of next-day S&P 500 returns conditional on VIX/VIX3M changes or inversions: none found (only practitioner pages). No source documents equity-direction predictability from the slope change; the prereg relies on the variance-equity correlation bridge.
prior: Very weak. The documented effect is a variance risk premium, which is compatible with equities NOT moving predictably (premium earned by variance sellers). A same-day equity reversal after a VIX spike ('buy fear') and continuation are both folk beliefs. The slope is published after the close, so any equity reaction overnight (not tradeable here; RTH only) is lost.
closed_ideas_check: Closed list forbids 'anything with a VIX filter layered on a closed family'. Here the VIX-term-structure change IS the signal (no closed base rule: entry at 09:35, flat at 15:55, no levels, no ORB/VWAP/momentum). Distinct from the closed implied-move band fade (level of implied move, fade at bands) and from V1/V2 (intraday QQQ options). Families not in data_spend_ledger.
timestamp_semantics: bar['daily'] = Cboe closes dated the PREVIOUS ES session (frozen eval; LOG iteration 3a/3b), so VIX/VIX3M(prev) and the stored VIX/VIX3M of the session before are both known before today's open. The decision is taken on slot 0's close (09:35) only because the engine acts on bar closes; no intraday option data is used.
features: D = VIX/VIX3M at the previous session's close minus the same ratio one session earlier (both from bar['daily'] of consecutive sessions)
(derived) A = D - mean of D over the prior 52 sessions with the SAME weekday as today (needs >= 40), removing the VIX weekend-quoting calendar pattern
(derived) z = A / sd(A over the prior 60 sessions, n-1; needs >= 40)

rules.bars: 5m RTH bars; decision at bar close, fills from the next bar.
rules.sessions: skip half days; a session whose bar['daily'] lacks VIX or VIX3M, or whose previous session lacked them, gives no D (and no history entry).
rules.history: D is stored for every session with a D (traded or not, half days included since D is a prior-close quantity); A is stored once the weekday mean exists.
rules.entry: on slot 0's close: if |z| >= Z (Z = 0 means any nonzero z), market order at the next bar's open (09:35); side = -sign(z) (ratio fell -> long; ratio rose -> short).
rules.risk: stop = c[0] - side * 1.0 * ADR20, ADR20 = mean ES RTH (high - low) of the prior 20 completed full sessions. Fixed.
rules.exit: the engine's flat at the 15:55 open, or the stop.

deviation_from_plan: (1) Ratio fixed to VIX/VIX3M (VIX9D/VIX not used: 1 feature budget slot, and VIX/VIX3M is closer to Johnson's 1-vs-3-month slope). (2) The plan asks to report whether the signal is just day-of-week: the count-only scan of the RAW change showed a strong weekday pattern (long share Mon 0.68, Tue 0.33-0.37 at every Z), which side-matched twins would not neutralise, so the signal is weekday-adjusted. After adjustment, long share by weekday is 0.41-0.55. (3) Product ES (VIX is SPX-based).
count_only_scan: ES dev, 1,986 trade sessions. Raw D: Z 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 -> 1,945 / 1,072 / 484 / 227 sessions. Weekday-adjusted z (this rule): 1,747 / 961 / 449 / 205; long share 0.51 / 0.51 / 0.48 / 0.45. The weekday mean needs ~10 months of history, so 2011 trades start around November 2011. No futures return was computed.
walk_forward: fixed: no selection; all three Z judged by the frozen dev gate on 'dev' (ES 2011-02..2018-12), each needing its grid neighbours positive.
rejection_evidence: Reject if the frozen dev gate fails for every Z. Report, not gate: mean R long vs short; by weekday; by ratio level (inverted > 1 vs contango); per-year; mean R with the RAW (unadjusted) side for comparison is NOT computed (that would be a second rule).
